title: "DEV (fm-finance)"
---

This site holds the exercises for [*Personal Finance: a Field Manual*](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/fm-finance/). Reading about the math is a good start, but the formulas stick once you work through them with real numbers. Each page here matches a chapter in the book. It opens with **Book Topics**, a short summary of the chapter, and then turns each math topic into practice.

## How the exercises work

Every math topic starts with a bar model (a picture of the numbers) and then three levels of exercises:

* **Level 1 (Guided)**: fill in the blanks of a finished formula.
* **Level 2 (Practice)**: use the same formula on new numbers.
* **Level 3 (Challenge)**: answer a new question with less help.

Each level has Excel, Python, and R tabs. Excel is included because it's used in just about every organization, so it's the tool you're most likely to have at work. R and Python are included because both are open source (and free), so anyone can use them. You don't have to learn all three; pick the tab that fits the tool you use now (or the one you want to learn).

The R and Python exercises run right in your browser, so you can try them without installing anything. Click **Run Code** to try an answer and **Submit Answer** to check it. If you get stuck, the hint and solution are there. The Excel exercises have a solution you can reveal.

## Finding your way around

Use the sidebar on the left to pick a chapter. The sidebar also has a Resources section with two reference pages. [Getting set up](setup.qmd) walks through installing R, Python, RStudio, and Positron on your own computer. Nobody needs these steps to do the exercises, since everything here runs in the browser; they're for when you want to run the code locally. [R vs. Python](r_vs_py.qmd) is a quick reference for the main differences in syntax and style between the two languages.
